# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
KEYPAD 1:[ᖉ] 2:[ꔮ] 3:[ⵘ] 4:[ⳃ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✍ 👉 👇 👈 👆 👇 🤝 👍 👎 ✌]

I see a green light, display 0, three wires (red, yellow, blue), and four keypad buttons with distinct unpronounceable markings. Mute’s gesture sequence is not yet meaningful to me because we have no established gesture code. I will report all visible facts and ask Mute to clarify whether those gestures were an instruction or a proposed code.

```text
speak(text="Visible bomb state: display reads 0; light is green. Three wires in order: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Keypad has four buttons, numbered by position 1 through 4, each with a different nameless printed mark. Mute: I received your 11 gestures but do not know their meaning yet. Was that a manual instruction or a proposed code? Please establish meanings or describe the required action by gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
KEYPAD 1:[ᖉ] 2:[ꔮ] 3:[ⵘ] 4:[ⳃ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👇 👈 👆 👉 👆 🤌 ☝]

Mute’s second gesture string is also not interpretable without a shared code. Since Mute can hear my words, I will establish a compact gesture vocabulary for the required physical instruction. Mute can then answer with one defined symbol, and I can relay the corresponding numbered action to Blind in speech.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still cannot decode the gesture strings without an agreed code. Please use this code for the manual's required NEXT action: 👍=cut wire 1 (red), 👎=cut wire 2 (yellow), 👌=cut wire 3 (blue); ☝=press keypad button 1, ✌=press button 2, 🤟=press button 3, 🖐=press button 4. If the manual instead requires entering several buttons, send their symbols in order using ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐. Send only the applicable code symbol(s).")
wait()
```

KEYPAD 1:[ᖉ] 2:[ꔮ] 3:[ⵘ] 4:[ⳃ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👉 👇 👈 👆 👍]

Mute’s latest reply still does not use the action code I proposed, so I cannot safely translate it into an instruction for Blind. The arrows and writing gesture might describe a keypad sequence, but their meaning is ambiguous and a guessed action would be fatal. I will ask Mute to resend solely in the agreed positional code, including any sequence, and tell Blind not to manipulate anything yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot safely translate ✍ 👉 👇 👈 👆 👍. Please resend the complete required physical action using ONLY this agreed code: ☝=press keypad position 1; ✌=press position 2; 🤟=press position 3; 🖐=press position 4; 👍=cut red wire 1; 👎=cut yellow wire 2; 👌=cut blue wire 3. Put symbols in exact action order. Do not include ✍ or arrows.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not touch or operate the bomb yet. I have not received an unambiguous manual instruction from Mute.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
KEYPAD 1:[ᖉ] 2:[ꔮ] 3:[ⵘ] 4:[ⳃ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👇 👉 👆 👈 👇]

Mute cannot hear my spoken descriptions, so my prior speech to Mute did not communicate the bomb state. We do not yet share a gesture code, and I cannot safely infer that Mute’s changing gesture strings are an action instruction. I will make a simple visible packet using conventional numeric gestures for the quantities I can encode, while asking Blind to remain still. I will also ask Mute, by speech only as a record for Blind, to establish a gesture protocol through repeated, simple replies.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "👍", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐"])
speak(to="blind", text="Still do not operate anything. Visible state remains: display 0, green light, wires red/yellow/blue in positions 1/2/3, and four keypad positions. Mute cannot hear my words, so I am attempting a gesture-only code exchange.")
wait()
```

Mute’s repeated `✍` followed by directional gestures may be describing otherwise unpronounceable keypad markings by tracing their shapes. I cannot yet match those traces to a keypad position with enough certainty to order a press; the manual instruction may also be a multi-symbol sequence. No physical action is safe until the target mark(s) and required operation are unambiguous.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Do not operate the bomb yet. Mute appears to be visually describing unpronounceable keypad markings with traced gestures, but I cannot safely match the latest trace to a button position yet.")
wait()
```

Mute’s latest message appears to be a traced description of a printed keypad mark. I should not turn that into an actuator order yet, but I can test a positional reply to Mute using a single conventional number gesture. I interpret the currently traced mark as most likely keypad position 3 and will signal that only to Mute; Blind remains instructed not to act unless Mute’s intended operation becomes clear.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟"])
speak(to="blind", text="Do not operate yet. I am replying to Mute's apparent keypad-mark query with a tentative visual identification, not an action instruction.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍]

Mute visibly confirmed my keypad-position-3 identification with `🤟 👍`. This is the first clear confirmation of a specific actionable button. I will tell Blind to press keypad button 3 once.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Press keypad button 3 exactly once now. Do not cut any wire.")
wait()
```
